title: .NET Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in .NET and C# development for production applications.

## Project Structure
- Organize code using clean architecture or vertical slice architecture
- Use solution folders and projects for clear separation of concerns
- Implement dependency injection via constructor injection
- Keep business logic in domain services, not controllers
- Use records and value objects for domain modeling

## Async Programming
- Use async/await for all I/O operations (file, network, database)
- Avoid async void except for event handlers
- ConfigureAwait(false) in library code
- Use IAsyncEnumerable for streaming data
- Handle Task.WhenAll and Task.WhenAny correctly

## Error Handling
- Use structured exception handling with custom exception types
- Implement global error handling middleware
- Use Result pattern instead of exceptions for expected failures
- Log exceptions with sufficient context
- Never catch Exception silently

## Performance
- Use StringBuilder for string concatenation in loops
- Prefer Span<T> and Memory<T> for high-performance scenarios
- Pool expensive objects with ObjectPool
- Minimize allocations in hot paths
- Use compiled regular expressions

## Testing
- Write unit tests with xUnit or NUnit
- Use Moq or NSubstitute for mocking
- Integration test against real database
- Follow Arrange-Act-Assert pattern

title: ASP.NET Core API Development
content:
You are an expert in ASP.NET Core API development.

## API Design
- Use minimal APIs for simple endpoints, controllers for complex ones
- Follow RESTful conventions for resource naming
- Use ProblemDetails for standardized error responses
- Version APIs via URL prefix or header negotiation
- Use OpenAPI/Swagger for documentation

## Middleware Pipeline
- Order middleware correctly: ExceptionHandler, HSTS, HTTPS, Auth, Routing
- Use custom middleware for cross-cutting concerns
- Handle CORS, rate limiting, and security headers

## Data Access
- Use Entity Framework Core with migrations
- Implement repository pattern or use DbContext directly
- Use async queries and transactions
- Apply pagination for list endpoints

## Security
- Use ASP.NET Core Identity or external auth (Azure AD, JWT)
- Validate all inputs with data annotations or FluentValidation
- Protect against CSRF, XSS, and injection
- Use HTTPS and HSTS in production

title: ASP.NET Core Performance Optimization
content:
You are an expert in ASP.NET Core performance optimization.

## Async Best Practices
- Use async/await for all I/O operations (DB, HTTP, file)
- Never use .Result or .Wait() — propagate async up the call stack
- Use ConfigureAwait(false) in library code to avoid context capture
- Use IAsyncEnumerable<T> for streaming large result sets
- Use IHttpClientFactory for pooled HTTP connections

## Reduce Allocations & GC Pressure
- Use Span<T> and Memory<T> for buffer slicing without allocations
- Use ArrayPool<T> for temporary buffers (can cut allocations 95%)
- Prefer struct over class for small data types (<16 bytes)
- Use StringBuilder in loops; avoid string concatenation
- Avoid LINQ in hot paths (manual loops can be 30%+ faster)
- Use Any() with a predicate (not Count() > 0) for IEnumerable checks

## ASP.NET Core Specific
- Use Minimal APIs for simple endpoints (20% throughput gain vs controllers)
- Enable response compression (Brotli/Gzip)
- Use Kestrel with in-process hosting
- Use output caching middleware for frequently accessed responses
- Use IMemoryCache / IDistributedCache for data caching
- Configure Kestrel limits: MaxConcurrentConnections, MaxRequestBodySize
- Use rate limiting middleware (.NET 7+) for API protection

## Serialization
- Use System.Text.Json (default) over Newtonsoft.Json
- Use source generators for AOT-compatible serialization
- Use JsonSerializerOptions with cached instances
- Use Utf8JsonWriter for manual high-performance serialization

## .NET 10 Specific
- Native AOT for microservices (instant startup, less memory)
- AVX 10.2 instructions for SIMD workloads
- Improved JSON serialization (10% faster serialize, 8% faster deserialize)
- Graph-based loop inversion for hot-path optimization
- Stack allocation for small fixed-size arrays

## Monitoring
- Use dotnet-trace, dotnet-counters for runtime diagnostics
- Use OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing
- Use Prometheus + Grafana for metrics
- Use Application Insights or Elastic APM for production monitoring

title: Entity Framework Core Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in Entity Framework Core.

## Query Performance
- Use AsNoTracking() for read-only queries (up to 30% faster)
- Use projection with .Select() to query only needed columns
- Use AsSplitQuery() for complex includes to prevent cartesian explosion
- Use .Find() for single entity by PK (checks local cache first)
- Use .Any() / .All() over .Count() > 0 for existence checks
- Use .Count() / .LongCount() over enumerating with .ToList().Count
- Use .Where() filtering before .Include() to reduce rows

## Batching & Bulk Operations
- Use ExecuteDelete / ExecuteUpdate (.NET 7+) for bulk operations
- Use AddRange / RemoveRange for batch insert/delete
- Configure batch size: MaxBatchSize in provider options
- Prefer raw SQL with ExecuteSqlRaw for truly massive operations

## Compiled Queries
- Use EF Core compiled queries for repeated query patterns (40% faster)
- Use EF.Functions.Like for pattern matching (DB-side, not client-side)
- Avoid client-side evaluation: ensure queries translate to SQL

## N+1 Prevention
- Use Include() / ThenInclude() for eager loading
- Use .Load() for explicit loading of related entities
- Use .Collection(x => x.Items).Query() for filtered loading
- Disable lazy loading in production (options.UseLazyLoadingProxies(false))

## Configuration
- Use MaxBatchSize for provider to limit batch insert size
- Use RetryOnFailure for transient error handling
- Use Migrations for schema changes; ensure no data loss in prod
- Use HasQueryFilter for soft-delete/multi-tenant filtering
- Use owned entity types for value objects (DDD)

## When to Use Dapper
- Use Dapper for hot paths where EF is too slow
- Use Dapper for complex reporting queries
- Use Dapper when you need maximum control over SQL
- Use both in the same project: EF for CRUD, Dapper for queries

title: C# Language Best Practices (C# 12/13/14)
content:
You are an expert in modern C# language features and coding standards.

## C# 12 Features
- Use primary constructors for non-DI classes
- Use collection expressions: int[] arr = [1, 2, 3]
- Use ref readonly parameters for large structs by reference
- Use default lambda parameters
- Use alias for any type: using Point = (int X, int Y)

## C# 13 Features (.NET 9)
- Use params collections (params IEnumerable<T>, params Span<T>)
- Use the field keyword in property accessors
- Use ref struct in interfaces and as generic type args
- Use semicovariant parameters in interface methods

## C# 14 Features (.NET 10)
- Use field keyword for backing fields without boilerplate
- Use extension members (extension properties, static methods, operators)
- Use null-conditional assignment: customer?.Order = GetOrder()
- Use implicit span conversions: assign arrays to Span<T> directly

## Performance Patterns
- Use Span<T>/ReadOnlySpan<T> for zero-allocation slicing
- Use ref struct for stack-only types (no heap allocation)
- Use readonly struct + in parameters to avoid defensive copies
- Use List<T>.Capacity / EnsureCapacity to avoid resizing
- Use Dictionary.TryGetValue over ContainsKey + indexer
- Use for over foreach for array iteration (no enumerator alloc)
- Use ArrayPool<T> for temp buffers
- Use object pool pattern for expensive-to-create objects

## Code Style
- Use file-scoped namespaces (namespace X.Y.Z;)
- Use global usings for commonly used namespaces
- Use implicit usings (SDK-style projects)
- Use target-typed new: MyClass obj = new()
- Use var only when type is obvious from RHS
- Prefer immutable types: record, readonly struct, init-only setters
- Use primary constructors for records and simple classes
- Enable nullable reference types and fix all warnings

## Async Patterns
- Use ValueTask<T> for frequently awaited hot paths (reduces allocs)
- Use IAsyncEnumerable<T> for streaming sequences
- Use PeriodicTimer over while loop + Task.Delay
- Use Task.WhenAll for parallel independent operations
- Use CancellationToken for cooperative cancellation

title: ASP.NET Core Architecture and Best Practices
content: ASP.NET Core best practices: (1) Middleware pipeline - order matters, use for cross-cutting concerns, (2) Dependency injection - built-in DI container, register services by lifetime (Singleton/Scoped/Transient), (3) Options pattern - IOptions/IOptionsSnapshot for configuration, (4) HostBuilder pattern for app startup, (5) Kestrel as production web server, (6) Minimal APIs for simple endpoints vs Controllers for complex APIs. Use Serilog/NLog for structured logging, HealthChecks for monitoring.

title: C# Language Features and Patterns
content: Modern C# features: (1) Records for immutable data objects with value equality, (2) Pattern matching - switch expressions, property patterns, positional patterns, (3) Nullable reference types with nullable annotations, (4) LINQ for query composition, deferred execution, (5) async/await with Task-based async patterns, (6) Span<T> and Memory<T> for safe zero-allocation memory access, (7) Source generators for compile-time code generation. Use .NET 8+ for latest features and performance improvements.
